_doc: One business's AEO and SEO settings. Names of things only: no key, no token.

goal._doc: What this function is for. Every other number on the read is a means to this one.
goal.measure: inbound leads from Google and from AI engines, counted by the CRM sales agent

site_changes._doc: How a fix reaches the site. pull_request: the business owns the site's code and the owner merges. package: someone else runs the site; the fix is a file set with its checks, handed over. A direct write to a live site is the owner's yes.
site_changes.who_applies: the owner, in the site's own repo

business.what_it_does: helps people and business owners find funding
business.buyer: People and businesses asking for funding; wholesalers; local businesses

rankspot._doc: The engine checker. One workspace per site. The key is read from the environment by name; prices are RankSpot's listed ones on the date below and are checked again before the owner's yes.
rankspot.daily_run: off until the owner's yes; once on, RankSpot bills each question on each platform every day by itself

google._doc: The search terms the business wants the front page for, buying terms first. Each: the term, its intent (buy, compare or learn), the page that answers it, and the video that answers it. Rank comes from the site's own Search Console, read through RankSpot.
spots: the AI answer at the top

video._doc: Video is the first choice for a buying term. This function writes the brief and places the finished video; the content function makes it. brief_holds is this function's reading of 'stuff that's going to convert, not just any video'.
brief_holds: the buyer's question as the title, in their words
the answer in the first 30 seconds
one next step: the call or page in goal.points_to, said and in the description's first line
placed: embedded on the page that answers the same question, with video schema
video._note: AI answers cite YouTube on most of the funding questions: one video per guide question, the existing answer pages as the scripts' source
video._pillars: The buying terms and the panel questions are drawn from the eight education pillars in campaigns/find-me-money/MESSAGING.md.

panel._doc: The questions a buyer asks an AI, each with where it came from. The panel's size is what the daily run costs.
panel._note: the measured baseline: named on 0 of 15 questions

spend._doc: The owner sets these. The cap covers the daily run and articles together; RankSpot's prepaid credit runs out behind it.

read.when: weekly, the same day each week, in the business's time zone

fixes._doc: Which fixes the engine chooses from. Each goes to the role that does it as a brief. Buying questions are listed first.

medium.publisher: the owner; publishing is his yes

audit_offer.note: the audit of a prospect's AI visibility is a sales offer; off until the owner prices it and says which function runs it
